class.name: SnowAvalanche3D
class.brief_description: Slab avalanches: release by the stability index, a Voellmy run-out on the snow cover's grid, entrainment and deposits.
class.description: Watches the [SnowCover3D] it belongs to (which adds it while [member SnowCover3D.avalanches_enabled]). The slab is the new snow since it last bonded (a week), or the snow over a buried crust. Where the stability index, the weak layer's shear strength (Jamieson and Johnston 2001, growing as it sinters) over the slab's shear stress (Foehn 1987), drops below 1 on slopes between [member min_slope] and [member max_slope], the slab releases, and the fracture runs through the neighbouring slab while it stays near failure. The released snow runs as a depth-averaged Voellmy flow (Voellmy 1955; Salm 1993; RAMMS, Christen et al. 2010). Gravity pulls it down the snow surface, against dry friction [member mu] and turbulent friction set by [member xi]. Its mass and momentum move cell to cell, it entrains the new snow it runs over at [member entrainment], and it deposits where it can no longer overcome its own friction. Snow surfaces near the camera break into blocks ([method SnowClumps3D.drop]). The moving snow stays in the cover's cells while it runs, so the snow map, [SnowSurface3D], plants and [WorldSnow] readers all see it move, and no snow is made or lost. Free rigid bodies in its path take its dynamic pressure, 1/2 rho u².

method.name: get_deposited_volume
method.description: m³ of debris the last avalanche left.

method.name: get_entrained_volume
method.description: m³ of snow the last avalanche picked up on its way.

method.name: get_flow_height_at
method.description: The flowing snow's depth at a point, m (0 when none runs).

method.name: get_flow_velocity_at
method.description: The flow's velocity at a point, m/s.

method.name: get_max_speed
method.description: The fastest the last avalanche ran, m/s.

method.name: get_recent_snow_at
method.description: The new snow since it last bonded at a point, m: the slab that can release.

method.name: get_run_out
method.description: How far the last avalanche's front got from the middle of its release, m.

method.name: stability_index
method.description: Foehn's (1987) stability index of a slab [param slab] m deep at [param slab_density] on [param slope] (radians), over a weak layer of [param weak_density] that has sintered [param age_hours]: below 1 it fails.

method.name: step
method.description: Runs the flow [param delta] seconds now (tests, cut scenes).

method.name: trigger
method.description: Releases whatever slab lies within [param radius] of [param at] on avalanche terrain, stable or not (a skier, a cornice falling, an explosive). Returns [code]true[/code] if one runs.

method.name: weak_layer_strength
method.description: Shear strength of a weak layer, Pa: 14.5 (rho / rho_ice)^1.73 kPa (Jamieson and Johnston 2001), growing by its age over two days as it sinters.

members.member: The snow the flow takes from the new snow it runs over, m per m/s of speed per second, above 5 m/s.
The steepest slope a slab releases on, degrees (steeper sheds as it falls).
The thinnest slab that releases by itself, m.
The gentlest slope a slab releases on, degrees.
Voellmy's dry friction (RAMMS: 0.155 for large avalanches to 0.4 for small ones).
If [code]true[/code], slabs release by themselves when the stability index fails; [method trigger] works either way.

signal.name: avalanche_released
signal.description: A slab released: the middle of the release and its volume, m³.

signal.name: avalanche_stopped
signal.description: The flow stopped: the middle of its release, the debris volume, m³, and how far it ran, m.
